title: [Bug]  sglang hangs before server readiness when launched under Nsight Systems process-tree profiling
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


When `sglang serve` is launched directly as an Nsight Systems target, the SGLang
parent process starts but the server never reaches readiness and never opens
`127.0.0.1:30000`. Running the same `sglang serve` command outside Nsight starts
successfully.

This prevents collecting a normal process-tree Nsight Systems trace for SGLang
serving workloads.

### Reproduction

nsys profile \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=cpu \
  --force-overwrite=true \
  --duration=90 \
  --wait=all \
  -o traces/nsys/sglang-gap \
  sglang serve \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B \
    --attention-backend triton \
    --decode-log-interval 1
